capabilities: Render a one-line button row inside a code block that opens a path
Open folders in the OS file manager or terminal
Launch arbitrary CLI executables (zed, cursor, nvim) on a path
Define global default buttons with per-block override, extension, or disable
Expose a public API via globalThis.openers
disambiguation: Not a note-opening or navigation plugin; it opens folders and files in external apps outside Obsidian.
extras: Desktop only (spawns local executables) and manual installation only; the manifest notes it has not been reviewed by Obsidian staff.
intentEvidence: A typed replacement for hand-written [Dir](file:///…) links.
motivation: To replace hand-written [Dir](file:///…) links with a typed code block.
problem: Obsidian offers no built-in way to open a note's folder or file in the OS file manager, a terminal, or external editors like zed or cursor.

relations.evidence: any CLI that takes a path (zed <dir>, cursor <dir>)
any CLI that takes a path (zed <dir>, cursor <dir>)

summary: Code-block plugin that renders a row of buttons opening a folder or file in Finder, a terminal, or any CLI editor.
